newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania taps OTC market to speed up sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: Romania taps OTC market to speed up sell-offs.

text.p: Romania's main privatisation agency said on Friday it would use the local over-the-counter (OTC) market to speed up the planned sale of some 1,000 state firms by the end of the year.

"We will sell companies in which the State Ownership Fund (FPS) has less than 50 percent of share capital through special deals on OTC market," said Dan Predoiu, head of the FPS's department for privatisations through the OTC.

The FPS aims to sell at least five companies per day, Predoiu said. He did not say how many of the 1,000 companies up for sale were already listed on the local OTC market, which operates in five trading sessions per week.

He said the FPS decided to use special deals -- struck out of the market -- for the sell-offs, to avoid influencing the price during trading. The FPS has yet to set a date when the special deals will start.

FPS president Sorin Dimitriu said the agency, which has a controlling stake in more than 6,500 state firms up for eventual privatisation, would use "similar methods" for sell-offs on the Bucharest stock exchange.

The new centrist government has pledged to speed up privatisation of large sectors of the economy. Of more than 6,500 firms slated for privatisation in 1992, some 3,100 had been sold by the end of 1996.
